key_learning_outcomes.label: C
items: Students analyze how characters shape a plot, how themes develop, how narrators and point of view shift, and how poetic forms affect meaning and style.
Students explain informational text sections and features, analyze central ideas and authors’ purposes, and track arguments and rhetorical appeals.
Students paraphrase grade-level texts and compare how authors from different time periods address related topics.
Students write narratives, claims, and expository texts, follow grade-level conventions, research with multiple sources, and present orally.
Students use academic vocabulary, Greek and Latin roots and affixes, and context to determine connotative and denotative meanings, and use digital tools and media.

version_and_update_notes.standards_version: Florida's State Academic Standards (B.E.S.T.) English Language Arts, 2025
notes: Organization: by_grade (ELA.6 codes). The book introduces a 6th-8th grade band, but these benchmarks are grade 6, not a named course.
Benchmark statements extracted from the rule-adopted 2025 PDF (Ref-18865), printed pages 78-82. Clarifications, sample texts, and convention skill lists are not stored in standard text.
No foundational-reading benchmarks (ELA.6.F) are printed for grade 6. ELA.6.C.1.1 is not in the grade 6 list; writing benchmarks start at ELA.6.C.1.2.
